papers.canonical_title: CJRR-Net: A Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking for Future-View Selection in Human Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: CJRR-Net combines current-view pose observations, calibrated camera configurations and candidate-specific geometric reprojections to rank eight future camera views for human pose estimation. A Blender rollout illustrates repeated camera selection.
papers.screening_reason: A learned policy issues camera-selection commands that change the active Blender camera; subsequent rendered observations drive the next decision. This is graphics-environment control, although the main quantitative objective is perception rather than authoring.

screening_evidence.evidence: 44-step closed-loop Blender rollout: selected camera becomes active 25 frames later, and 43 successive observations follow preceding camera commands.

papers.analysis_target: Task-time learned future-view selector, specifically its repeated Blender camera-control demonstration; not pose-estimator training or animation creation.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Select one of eight cameras; activate it for the next observation
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Active camera in Blender 5.0.1 animated scene
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Each selected camera supplies the next rendered observation in a 44-step closed-loop demonstration.

task.evidence: Discrete camera switching in an animated Blender scene keeps a subject visible.
task.reasoning: View selection determines visualization, not creation of animation or simulated dynamics.

input_form.evidence: Current RGB image and known calibrated camera positions/orientations supply the decision.
input_form.reasoning: RGB is Image; supplied camera geometry is a 3D representation. Pose estimates are internal intermediates.

output.evidence: Argmax score selects camera index and current-to-selected camera command.
output.reasoning: A discrete camera designation is a structured specification consumed by Blender; no generated program is claimed.

model_type.evidence: MLPs, attention pooling and two cross-attention blocks form a non-language ranking network.
model_type.reasoning: The codebook offers LLM/VLM/Hybrid but no non-language vision policy; Unclear records a label mismatch, not missing architecture.

model_training.evidence: Ranker trained with classification, ranking and regret losses; frozen NLF and RootHead.
model_training.reasoning: Supervised ranker training is reported, but not foundation-model supervised fine-tuning; available labels do not describe from-scratch training.

planning.evidence: One next-view argmax; motion planning is future work.
planning.reasoning: No represented multi-step plan; a single action choice is not PO-1 planning.

workflow.evidence: Observe, rank, select and acquire next view repeatedly.

update_strategy.evidence: Each new observation yields scores and selects one candidate camera.
update_strategy.reasoning: Observation-driven camera candidate selection updates the active view.

verifier.evidence: MPJPE and future ground truth are offline metrics; rollout uses a selector rather than judging a prior action.
verifier.reasoning: No loop verifier; the ranking policy is not a critic of executed output.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Future images and annotations only for supervision/offline evaluation; next observation feeds policy.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Candidate scores are action logits, not assessments of prior execution.

feedback_observation.evidence: Successive input images follow preceding camera commands.

memory_time.evidence: Current-image selection is described; no retained episodic state is reported.
memory_time.reasoning: Full text and memory search do not establish memory lifetime.

memory_reach.evidence: No agent memory store or access scope described.
memory_reach.reasoning: Cannot infer local/global memory merely from a single controller.

action_type.evidence: A selected camera index commands the next active view.
action_type.reasoning: Structured camera designation; native script/tool-call syntax is not specified.

graphics_software.evidence: Blender demonstration routes policy commands into active camera selection and observations.
graphics_software.reasoning: Custom policy-to-Blender closed-loop integration adapts the general environment.

tools.evidence: Frozen NLF-S and ViTPose extract pose and uncertainty from current images.
tools.reasoning: Invoked perception capabilities, not just offline metrics.

resources.evidence: Renderpeople animated human and FBX dance animation used in the rollout.

representation.evidence: Calibrated 3D joints/cameras and rendered RGB observations.
representation.reasoning: Geometry for cameras/pose; Pixels for rendered feedback. Animated state is not authored by selector.

papers.contribution: Candidate-specific geometry improves future camera selection; a qualitative closed-loop Blender demonstration establishes actual camera control.
papers.limitations: Quantitative evaluation uses one held-out subject and fixed camera configurations; potential NLF pretraining overlap. Closed-loop evidence is qualitative and does not establish authoring or continuous camera motion.
taxonomy_delta: Monitor a non-language learned controller label and supervised training-from-scratch label: current model labels do not cover the reported ranker.

papers.canonical_title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
papers.abstract: OnlyAct extracts scene-invariant action embeddings from V-JEPA 2 through label-free contrastive low-rank adaptation and evaluates their expressiveness, scene invariance, and ability to control autoregressive video world models.
papers.screening_reason: Explicit reusable action interface for interactive video world models, evaluated with camera/game action commands, but no closed-loop task agent is evaluated. Classify the enabling encoder, not a nonexistent planner.
screening_evidence: §3 pp4–7 defines action as agent- or camera-caused change; §3.3 and Figure3 support demonstration transfer and direct action control; Appendix D p20 explicitly limits evidence to offline evaluations.
papers.analysis_target: Enabling component: frozen adapted OnlyAct action encoder at inference, producing transferable latent control signals from demonstration frame pairs. Contrastive adaptation and downstream AdaWorld generation are described separately.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: External agent/camera action stream, or supplied demonstration; no task-time autonomous controller evaluated
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Map demonstrated or real actions into a reusable latent action interface
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Defines action as change caused by agent or camera, and explicitly evaluates real-action control of Minecraft, DMLab and Habitat video generation. Long-horizon closed-loop interaction is future work.

task.evidence: Representation enables action-conditioned video world simulators.
task.reasoning: Simulation is the explicitly supported downstream graphics purpose of the enabling component.

input_form.evidence: Consecutive demonstration frame pair is encoded as a two-frame video clip.

output.evidence: Single forward pass emits normalized 640-dimensional action embedding.
output.reasoning: A latent vector is not clearly any of Program/Structured Specification/Graphics Artifact/Rendered Media; do not substitute downstream generated video.

model_type.evidence: Main encoder is V-JEPA 2 ViT-L; Qwen embedding ablation is superseded. No agent decision-maker in encoder.
model_type.reasoning: Model type concerns agentic decision-maker, absent in this enabling component; not VLM merely because an alternative uses Qwen.

model_training.evidence: Encoder receives self-supervised contrastive LoRA adaptation; no task-agent decision model trained.
model_training.reasoning: Not Applicable to decision-maker axis; record encoder adaptation in notes rather than mislabel as supervised agent fine-tuning.

planning.evidence: Single forward pass; no prompts or trajectory optimization.

workflow.evidence: Frame clip encoding, pooling, fixed projection and normalization.
workflow.reasoning: Ordered inference pipeline, not a branched agent harness.

update_strategy.evidence: Frozen encoder outputs each action once.

verifier.evidence: Probes, scene reconstruction and action classifiers are offline evaluation.

feedback_assessment.reasoning: Final metrics do not affect subsequent encoder actions.

feedback_observation.evidence: Supplied frame pair is input, not feedback from an encoder-selected action.

memory_time.evidence: Per-pair encoding; six-frame context belongs to separate world model.
memory_time.reasoning: Stateless encoder has no agent memory; do not import generator context.

memory_reach.evidence: No shared agent memory in one-pass encoder.
memory_reach.reasoning: No memory subsystem to assign reach.

action_type.evidence: Continuous latent action vector conditions denoiser.
action_type.reasoning: Dense learned control is not clearly a structured specification or tool call in current codebook.

graphics_software.evidence: World model explicitly accepts a continuous per-transition action interface.
graphics_software.reasoning: Enabling interface is built for controllable world-state transitions; agent-ready access, not native GUI scripting.

tools.evidence: Foundation video encoder converts frames into action representations.
tools.reasoning: Callable visual analysis capability; RAFT training augmentation is not included as inference tool.

resources.evidence: Demonstration video supplies action stream transferable to other scenes.
resources.reasoning: Reusable demonstration trajectories, not benchmark examples silently counted as resources.

representation.evidence: Pixel frame pairs map to learned 640-dimensional normalized embeddings.
representation.reasoning: Pixels for supplied observations; Learned State for latent actions.

papers.contribution: Extracts transferable action signals from a pretrained video encoder without a reconstruction bottleneck, enabling action-conditioned video simulation.
papers.limitations: Offline evaluation only; action labels still required for direct-control alignment. Static-camera flow swaps and small contrastive batches limit adaptation; scene disentanglement is not guaranteed. Single world-model training seeds limit variance claims.
taxonomy_delta: Monitor latent-action interface/output labels for explicitly agent-facing world-model components; avoid forcing latent vectors into code/specification labels.

papers.abstract: UGG jointly models RGB video, depth and camera rays by conditional completion, with inference-time hypothesis selection using geometric evidence from RGB.
papers.screening_reason: Hypothesis sampling and geometric verification provide a concrete transferable graphics search mechanism, but no agent chooses graphics tools or acts on an environment. An embodied-agent motivation and best-of-N selection do not establish a deployed graphics agent.
screening_evidence: §3.4 pp5–6 and Appendix B.8 pp21–23 define numerical candidate selection; checklist p31 explicitly states agents are not core method components.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time geometric hypothesis search/verification for depth and camera reconstruction; not the separate camera-conditioned video generation configuration or training.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: Fixed numerical candidate selector; no demonstrated agent controller
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Rank independent depth/pose hypotheses using reprojection evidence
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Reconstructed scene depth and camera geometry
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Up to 16 scene hypotheses are scored and selected with RAFT correspondences and photometric/feature consistency. No agent-environment interaction is demonstrated; potential use is a verifier/search component.

task.evidence: Search selects depth and camera pose estimates.
task.reasoning: Reconstruction of geometric scene properties is modeling, not animation merely because input is video.

input_form.evidence: Full RGB video or first-last video frames condition geometry search.

output.evidence: Selected depth and camera geometry may come from independent candidates.
output.reasoning: Selected geometric reconstruction is the output artifact; generated RGB intermediates are not a second output for this subsystem.

model_type.evidence: Fixed candidate verifier; generative diffusion model supplies hypotheses; no agent decision model.
model_type.reasoning: Not Applicable to agent decision-maker model axis; diffusion is not a VLM controller.

model_training.evidence: Wan transformer fine-tuned for conditional generation; selector uses fixed rules.
model_training.reasoning: Generator fine-tuning must not be attributed to an absent decision-making agent.

planning.evidence: Sample, score, select; no task plan.
planning.reasoning: Best-of-N inference is not explicit planning.

workflow.evidence: Generate candidates then calculate residuals and select.
workflow.reasoning: Ordered processing stages; independent candidates do not alone establish concurrent scheduling.

update_strategy.evidence: Select candidate with lowest task-specific verification score.

verifier.evidence: Numerical reprojection and angular consistency verifier controls selected output.
verifier.reasoning: Programmatic check, not a model critic.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Depth residuals ranked per pair; pose mean angular discrepancy; argmin selects final candidate.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Ranking for depth and Score for pose both directly affect output selection, unlike final oracle metrics.

feedback_observation.evidence: Observed RGB correspondences and photometric evidence verify candidates.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Visual evidence rather than execution runtime or simulator state.

memory_time.evidence: Candidate pool is transient; agent memory lifetime not defined. History guidance is conditioning, not an agent memory store.
memory_time.reasoning: Reviewed methods and appendix do not warrant an agent memory label.

memory_reach.evidence: No role-scoped or shared agent memory architecture.

action_type.evidence: Internal numerical selection, no emitted graphics program, tool call or GUI action.

graphics_software.evidence: Tensor geometry prediction and OpenCV computations, no agent-adapted authoring environment.
graphics_software.reasoning: Graphics software readiness classification does not apply to absent agent interface.

tools.evidence: RAFT/DINOv2 extract visual evidence; reprojection residuals check sampled geometry.
tools.reasoning: Perception models extract evidence; Static Validator measures consistency without modifying geometry.

resources.evidence: Search uses supplied observations and pretrained models, no retrieved examples/assets/rules resource.
resources.reasoning: Training/evaluation datasets are not task-time reusable resources of search.

representation.evidence: Latent tokens decode to RGB, depth and camera rays.
representation.reasoning: Learned State for diffusion hypotheses; Pixels for RGB evidence; Geometry for depth/cameras.

papers.contribution: Joint generative geometry permits candidate diversity and RGB-grounded verification without ground-truth geometry at selection time.
papers.limitations: Reprojection proxy is imperfect, gains uneven, depth and pose may be selected from inconsistent candidates. No graphics-agent demonstration. Fine-tuning is expensive and confidence intervals are not reported.
taxonomy_delta: Borderline numerical hypothesis search should remain distinct from autonomous agent planning.

papers.canonical_title: TaoMate-R1: Temporal Role Specialization for Streaming Multi-Reference Video Generation
papers.abstract: A streaming multi-reference audiovisual diffusion generator allocates separate low-rank adapters to scene opening and continuation, with shared generation/context-writing parameters within each temporal role.
papers.screening_reason: E2_NON_AGENTIC. Full text resolves the provisional streaming-state lead as generator parameter sharing, not agentic control. Absolute chunk index alone selects opening/continuation adapters; external instructions condition synthesis. No material agent-facing interface or controller contribution beyond ordinary conditional video generation is established.

screening_evidence.evidence: Role r(b)=first at b=0, cont otherwise. Changing instructions preserves continuation adapter. Related work mentions agent planning, but this study explicitly concerns adaptation parameters under fixed history retention.

papers.contribution: Temporal rather than operation-based LoRA sharing reduces instruction-boundary luminance jumps in streaming video.
papers.limitations: 32 cases, ten long streams with cached teacher audio and end-frame conditions; external baselines concatenate independently generated clips. No task agent evaluated. Not all text alignment/audio metrics improve.

papers.canonical_title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
papers.abstract: Elastic-WAM learns a spatiotemporal refinement-demand field that selects when to stop video refinement, denoising step size, and which future tokens to refresh for efficient robot control.
papers.screening_reason: Learned state-dependent decisions allocate computation to generated visual futures, a defensible transferable mechanism for graphics agents. Demonstrated outputs/actions are robot controls, not authored graphics or operations in a graphics environment; internal latent refinement alone is not promoted to core.
screening_evidence: §3.2–3.4 pp4–6 learned WHEN/HOW FAR/WHERE controls update latent future tokens; §4 pp6–8 evaluates manipulation only.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time learned refinement-demand controller within a frozen WAM, not the separate robot action policy or three-stage teacher training.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Stop or continue latent video refinement; choose denoising progression and exact-budget token mask
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Internal future-video representations used for robot control; no exposed graphics artifact
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Model selects 96 of 196 future tokens for refresh and caches others. Transfer to graphics authoring or an interactive graphics simulator is not evaluated.

task.evidence: Latent future refinement supports manipulation rather than an explicit graphics task.
task.reasoning: Cannot force internal future imagination into Modeling/Animation/Simulation/Visualization.

input_form.evidence: Field consumes recurrent state s; backbone accepts language, images and proprioception.
input_form.reasoning: Do not attribute raw backbone input modalities directly to field; internal latent state lacks a codebook input label.

output.evidence: Commit probability, step size and token selection mask.
output.reasoning: Structured computation specification, not generated video or final robot trajectory.

model_type.evidence: Temporal and spatial branches predict field parameters; frozen backbone is joint video-action denoising model.
model_type.reasoning: No evidence field controller is LLM/VLM/Hybrid; codebook mismatch.

model_training.evidence: Three-stage action-grounded supervised learning with frozen WAM.
model_training.reasoning: Supervised controller learning reported, but not clearly fine-tuning a pretrained decision model; avoid conflating frozen backbone with off-the-shelf controller.

planning.evidence: Local recurrent refinement decisions; no represented task plan in field.
planning.reasoning: Replanning cycle belongs to robot execution, not field planning.

workflow.evidence: Dense initialization, repeated sparse refinement, then commit.

update_strategy.evidence: Refresh selected future queries, preserve unselected cached states.
update_strategy.reasoning: Local updates to a subset of latent representation.

verifier.evidence: Terminal action error supervises training; inference predicts demand.
verifier.reasoning: Training teacher/error must not be treated as task-time critic.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Demand probabilities guide action allocation; ground-truth errors only during training.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: No task-time feedback assessment of executed artifact.

feedback_observation.evidence: Updated recurrent latent state determines subsequent refinement.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Latent tensors are neither rendered Visual nor explicit structural scene state in the codebook.

memory_time.evidence: Hidden states, keys, values and last-refresh velocities reused across refinement steps within a replanning cycle.
memory_time.reasoning: Explicit within-run retained state; no cross-run memory claimed.

memory_reach.evidence: Layer-wise cache retained in the refinement/action denoising process.
memory_reach.reasoning: Local subsystem cache, not multi-agent global memory.

action_type.evidence: Emit commit, step progression, binary group mask.
action_type.reasoning: Structured control values; no code or tool API.

graphics_software.evidence: Internal neural computation, not graphics software control.
graphics_software.reasoning: Robot simulator is evaluation environment, not controlled authoring interface.

tools.reasoning: No callable graphics tools in this controller.

resources.evidence: Demonstrations train policies; no reusable assets/examples/rules accessed by task-time field reported.
resources.reasoning: Training data are not inference resources.

representation.evidence: Future-video latent tokens and layer-wise caches.

papers.contribution: A learned field jointly controls stopping, denoising progression and spatial refresh, reducing robot-policy inference latency without uniformly refining visual futures.
papers.limitations: Only manipulation evaluation; no graphics-agent demonstration. Robot success and latency do not establish visual fidelity. No explicit task-progress memory; authors' stage-discrimination explanation remains a hypothesis.
taxonomy_delta: Latent-computation control and non-language controllers strain input, model and feedback labels; keep this borderline rather than equating all world-model computation with graphics action.

papers.canonical_title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
papers.abstract: MetaWAM packs robot signals into fixed disjoint DCT channel bands within a unified latent meta-frame, allowing a pretrained video diffusion model to jointly predict robot actions, future observations and values without new learned interface modules.
papers.screening_reason: Compact structured action/world-model representation could inform graphics-simulator agent interfaces. Demonstrated controller operates a robot, not graphics authoring; numerical latent packing and future-view prediction do not establish agent-to-graphics action.
screening_evidence: §4 pp4–7 defines deterministic packing/masking; §5 pp7–9 and B.2 p14 evaluate robot actions, including physical Franka.
papers.analysis_target: Enabling representation: deterministic meta-frame pack/readout and slot routing at task time, rather than the downstream robot policy or video denoiser.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: MetaWAM robot policy; analytical interface itself has no autonomous controller
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Pack robot action/state/value signals and route their conditioning/target roles
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Video diffusion latent world representation; no authored graphics target demonstrated
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Interface preserves future-video prediction and robot actions; no experiment applies decisions to a graphics editor or world-construction environment.

task.evidence: Interface carries proprioception, action and value for joint world/action prediction.
task.reasoning: No clear graphics-purpose task label for robot latent-signal interface.

input_form.evidence: Normalized robot variables and one-hot task identifier are packed.
input_form.reasoning: Numeric robot signals are not covered by input form labels; do not import surrounding policy RGB/language.

output.evidence: Spatial latent meta-frame and analytic recovery of normalized signals.
output.reasoning: Latent carrier is not clearly an exposed graphics artifact/specification.

model_type.evidence: Fixed coefficient allocation and analytical DCT/iDCT; no learned interface parameters.

model_training.evidence: Packing introduces no learned parameters; full fine-tuning belongs to separate Cosmos backbone.
model_training.reasoning: Interface has no trained decision model.

planning.evidence: Deterministic mask from task type; no plan representation.

workflow.evidence: Normalize/pack, inverse transform, route, then transform/readout.

verifier.evidence: Frozen-denoiser compatibility is diagnostic evaluation, not task-time verification.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Relative errors, PSNR and action L1 are monitoring/evaluation.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Do not recast final metrics as loop scores.

feedback_observation.evidence: Packing/readout is analytical without environment feedback.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Policy observations are not feedback to this representation subsystem.

memory_time.evidence: Fixed stateless transform of current input signals.

memory_reach.evidence: No memory store or agent access permissions.

action_type.evidence: Mask is deterministically derived; no agent operation emitted.
action_type.reasoning: This subsystem is a representation, not graphics action execution.

graphics_software.evidence: Video diffusion latent interface; robot simulators only used in task evaluation.

tools.evidence: Analytic mathematical transforms, no graphics tool selection.
tools.reasoning: No callable graphics tools in selected unit.

resources.evidence: Predefined channel partition, fixed coefficient slots and task-specific mask rules reused.
resources.reasoning: Reusable schema/rules define interface; not training demonstrations.

representation.evidence: Signals are carried inside pretrained video latent frame space.
representation.reasoning: Learned State denotes carrier space; transform itself remains analytic.

papers.contribution: Distribution-aware spectral packing reduces latent sequence length while preserving jointly predicted robot signals and future visuals.
papers.limitations: Fixed layouts and loss weights may need retuning; limited language grounding and background robustness. No graphics-controller demonstration. Interface gains primarily evaluated through manipulation success.
taxonomy_delta: Dense latent control carriers are underrepresented in input/output labels; monitor without expanding scope to every robot policy.

papers.canonical_title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
papers.abstract: SplatLab autonomously proposes, implements and experimentally refines 3D Gaussian Splatting methods over verified baseline plugins using a cascade-weighted Elo tournament, standing falsifier, integrity audit and reviewer-driven re-experimentation.
papers.screening_reason: Implementation and evolutionary controllers edit executable neural-rendering programs, train and render them, and use observed metrics/build failures to change subsequent code. Graphics algorithm development is a concrete graphics-program action, not merely generic scientific discussion.
screening_evidence: §3 Stage3–4 pp5–6 specifies structured EVOLVE-BLOCK diffs, ns-train execution, GPU PSNR ranking, bounded debugger patches and falsifier vetoes.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time research-agent implementation/refinement loop (Stages3–4) that creates and edits 3DGS rendering/reconstruction code. Excludes manuscript/figure authoring and downstream training of generated 3DGS models from agent taxonomy.

papers.canonical_title: 3A-VLA: Abstraction-Aligned Action Learning for Vision-Language Agents in 3D Game Worlds
papers.abstract: 3A-VLA uses sparse intention and environmental affordance supervision plus abstraction-alignment reweighting to improve imitation-trained reactive game-playing policies.

events.evidence: Official metadata and canonical v2 history.

papers.screening_reason: E1_DOMAIN/E7_OUTSIDE_TASK_BOUNDARY. Full text demonstrates game-playing, combat and navigation, not graphics authoring, scene construction or world auditing. The fact that actions affect a rendered game does not alone establish a graphics research target; generic abstraction supervision is not a material graphics-specific enabling component.

screening_evidence.evidence: Task-time inference only outputs human-like game actions; Game for Peace tasks are parachuting/scavenging/combat/revival/vehicle/rotation. Minecraft reports aggregate embodied/combat/GUI scores but no graphics artifact authoring. IA/ESA are training-only, and policy lacks temporal memory.

papers.contribution: Task-agnostic sparse training abstractions improve reactive VLA game control and facilitate token pruning.
papers.limitations: No long-horizon planning or explicit temporal memory; ESA lacks terrain/collision geometry. Cross-game results concern short-horizon combat, not general completion or graphics tasks.

papers.canonical_title: Pose Distance Fields for Humanoid Robots
papers.abstract: PDF-HR learns a differentiable pose-plausibility distance prior for Unitree G1 and integrates it into robot motion tracking, mimicry and inverse-kinematics retargeting.
papers.screening_reason: Full text establishes a robot pose regularizer and humanoid tracking reward, not an agent controlling graphics authoring or an explicitly graphics-agent-facing component. Related physics-based character-control methods motivate it, but experiments target Unitree G1 behavior and physical deployment. The initially plausible animation connection remains generic motion-prior transfer, insufficient material graphics-agent evidence.

screening_evidence.evidence: 29-DoF robot joint vector maps to scalar distance; GMR/Mink solves IK, RL reward shapes robot tracking, and TextOp extension changes only low-level robot tracking reward. No graphics authoring controller is introduced.

papers.contribution: Lightweight pose-distance reward improves humanoid policy sample efficiency and regularizes retargeting.
papers.limitations: Some tracking accuracy regresses, style mimicry can collapse, retargeting can be slower and jitterier, and retargeted training poses may be physically infeasible. Single primary robot morphology.

papers.canonical_title: DORIS: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration
papers.abstract: DORIS uses RGB and polarization observations to predict degradation descriptions whose hidden states condition single-step latent underwater image restoration.
papers.screening_reason: E2_NON_AGENTIC/E3_ONE_SHOT. Diagnostic language hidden states provide conditioning to a single forward-pass restoration network, not a tool/action decision, agent-facing component or feedback controller. Provisional controller possibility resolved by explicit architecture. ChatGPT code assistance is authoring support, not an experimental graphics agent.

screening_evidence.evidence: Answer hidden states map through adapter into SD2 U-Net; fixed terminal timestep produces one velocity prediction in a single forward pass. LLM usage disclosure concerns grammar and implementation error assistance.

papers.contribution: Polarization-aware degradation descriptions and local RGB/polarization alignment improve single-step underwater restoration.
papers.limitations: Outdoor no-reference evaluation only; several small downstream gains and tradeoffs in SSIM/DISTS. Supplementary hyperparameter material referenced but not present in retrieved PDF.
